# sources/test-tools/syzkaller/pkg/report/testdata/linux/report/477

Purpose: Linux reporter parse fixture for syzkaller. It encodes the expected parsed title `BUG: corrupted list in ath9k_htc_wait_for_target`, expected type `MEMORY_SAFETY_BUG`, alternate titles `bad-access in ath9k_htc_wait_for_target`, corrupted flag `N`, and panicked flag `Y`. The source is a static kernel-console transcript, not executable test code; its job is to pin how the Linux reporter recognizes ath9k HTC target wait corrupted list. It has no explicit REPORT block, so the parser derives the report from the console transcript and expected headers.

Important APIs, types, and functions: this file is consumed by `pkg/report/report_test.go` through `testParseImpl`, `Reporter.ContainsCrash`, `Reporter.Parse`, and `Reporter.ParseFrom`. It exercises Linux reporter pattern tables and title extraction in `linux.go`, generic report shaping in `report.go`, and crash-type mapping through `pkg/report/crash.TitleToType`. Parser-relevant functions and symbols in the log include __list_del_entry_valid, wait_for_completion_timeout, ath9k_htc_wait_for_target, ath9k_htc_probe_device, request_firmware_work_func. Diagnostic tokens visible in the complete fixture include kernel panic, expected panicked.

Control flow: the test harness enumerates `pkg/report/testdata/linux/report`, reads expectation headers until the blank line or `REPORT:` marker, and feeds the remaining bytes to a Linux `Reporter`. For this fixture, `ContainsCrash` must match the expected crash, `Parse` must locate the first report span, and `ParseFrom` must rediscover the same crash from its start offset but not after its end offset. The log-specific flow is: list_debug BUG at __list_del_entry_valid during request_firmware_work_func, flowing through ath9k_htc_wait_for_target. There are 76 source lines; exact report-body comparison is `no`.

State and persistence behavior: all persistent state lives in this text file: header expectations, alternate titles, crash transcript bytes, and any explicit report body. During tests, state is transient parser output: crash start/end offsets, selected title, alternate titles, crash type, corruption/panic flags, guilty-file hints, and trimmed report bytes. The fixture performs no filesystem, network, device, or kernel mutation; it models those kernel-side events only as immutable input text.

Dependencies and integration points: the fixture integrates with syzkaller's Linux report recognizer, stack-frame skip lists, sanitizer parsers, lockdep/warning/hung-task detectors, panic handling, corruption handling, and report-boundary logic. Product-level consumers are crash deduplication, dashboard grouping, repro triage, maintainers' signal routing, and automated bisection. Because the source lives under `testdata/linux/report`, its filename is intentionally opaque; the headers and transcript are the behavioral contract.

Risks and edge cases: corrupted-list crashes must be grouped by the wireless driver path, not list_debug helpers. More generally, regressions can come from overfitting to timestamps, CPU/task prefixes, architecture-specific syscall wrappers, compiler suffixes such as `.cold` or `.constprop`, repeated helper frames, panic-on-warn trailers, allocation/free stacks, or noisy subsystem messages preceding the crash. Reports flagged as corrupted must remain conservative about title specificity, while non-crash logs must not be promoted just because they contain alarming words.

Test signals: a passing parser run returns title `BUG: corrupted list in ath9k_htc_wait_for_target`, type `MEMORY_SAFETY_BUG`, alternate titles `bad-access in ath9k_htc_wait_for_target`, corrupted `N`, panicked `Y`, and exact-body comparison `no`. It must keep the meaningful frame named by the expected title when the log provides one, avoid helper-only titles, preserve panic/corruption semantics, and produce stable output across `Parse` and `ParseFrom`.
